Good morning, everyone.
Today we are going to discuss the operating system, which is one of the most important components of a computer system.
We will learn about processes, threads, CPU scheduling, memory management, virtual memory and synchronization.
We will also understand how these concepts work together when we run applications on our computer.
Let us begin with the basic definition.
An operating system is a system software that acts as an intermediary between the user application programs and computer hardware.
It manages resources such as the CPU main memory, storage devices and input output devices.
Example of operating systems include Windows, Linux, Mac OS and Android.
The main purpose of an operating system is to make computer resources convenient, efficient and secure to use.
For example, when you open a web browser, play a video and download a file at the same time.
The operating system coordinates these activities and distributes resources among the running applications.
Now, let us understand the concept of a process.
A process is a program that is currently executing.
A program stored on a disk is passive.
Whereas, process is active because its inference structure are being executed by the CPU.
Every process has information associated with it.
Such as its process identifier, execution state, CPU registers and memory information.
The operating system stores important process related information in a data structure called process control block or PCB.
A process may be in the new, ready, running, waiting or terminated state.
A ready process is waiting for CPU time.
While a waiting process is waiting for an event such as the completion of an input output operation.
When the operating system stops one process and starts executing another, a context switch occurs.
During a context switch, the operating system saves the execution state of the current process and re-stores the state of the next process.
Context switching supports multitasking, although it also introduces overhead because the CPU spends time switching between processes instead of executing their instructions.
Next, let us discuss CPU scheduling.
CPU scheduling is the process of selecting a ready process for execution.
The first comes first of algorithm executes processes in the order in which they arrive.
Shortest Job First the process with the shortest expected CPU burst, round robin, assigned each process of fixed time quantum and then moves to the next ready process.
Shaddling algorithm are evaluated using cried area such as waiting time, turnaround time response time, CPU utilization.
Round robin is commonly associated with interactive systems because it provides processes with regular opportunities to execute.
However, choosing an appropriate time quantum is important.
If the time quantum is too small, context switching overhead may increase.
If it is too large, round robin may behave similarly to first come first of schedule them.
Now, let us move to the memory management.
The operating system allocates memory to processes and protects one process from accessing another processes private memory without permission.
One important technique is paging.
In paging logical memory is divided into fixed size blocks called pages, while physical memory is divided into blocks called frames.
Page table maps, virtual pages, two physical frames.
A translation look aside buffer or TLB stores recently used address translations to speed up memory access.
For required pages not currently available in physical memory or page fault occurs.
The operating system may need to load that page from secondary storage before execution can continue.
